# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| red flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | blue |
| 1 | red |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | red |
| 4 | yellow |
| 5 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Board now: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT is red again (it was yellow, now back to red). Wires still 1 yellow 2 blue 3 red. Mute, if you can hear this, please describe in words what the manual says to do, since I cannot interpret gestures alone.

Deaf explicitly cannot interpret my gestures at all, and is asking for spoken words — but I cannot speak, only gesture. I need to use Deaf's own proposed fallback: a fixed gesture code where tap count = wire number. I already sent two taps ("☝","☝") for wire 2, but Deaf's message doesn't acknowledge receiving that gesture code confirmation — perhaps it arrived but Deaf is still asking, or my gesture arrived after Deaf's message was already composed (turn ordering: Mute, Blind, Deaf — so my gesture from turn 4 should have reached Deaf before Deaf's turn 5 message... but the report shown is Deaf's turn 5 output, meaning Deaf already had my gesture but didn't mention it).

Since gestures alone convey ambiguity (blank vs symbol distinction only tells "something signaled" to non-seers, but Deaf CAN see gestures, just doesn't know their meaning without agreement). Deaf asked for a fixed code: "one tap for wire 1, two for wire 2, three for wire 3." I already sent two taps. I should resend more clearly, perhaps with repeated distinct symbol taps and confirm it multiple times, and also try a different approach: gesture the actual manual table content isn't decodable either without agreement.

Best: strictly follow Deaf's suggested code - send exactly two identical gesture symbols to mean "wire 2", clearly separated, and keep it simple/consistent since that's the only channel I have.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝"])
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT currently red (was yellow, toggling), wires 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red. What does the manual say to do for this light/display/wire combination? Please tell me which wire to cut.
Deaf says: Board now: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT yellow, wires 1 yellow 2 blue 3 red - same as two turns ago. Mute, since you can't be heard by Blind directly, please gesture a single tally count matching a wire number, like one symbol for wire 1, two symbols for wire 2, three for wire 3, so I can relay which wire to cut.

Now the picture is clear: Blind cannot hear me directly, only Deaf can see my gestures, and Deaf will relay by speech to Blind. Deaf explicitly confirmed the tally code: one symbol = wire 1, two symbols = wire 2, three = wire 3.

Now, what does the manual say? The light seems to be toggling between red and yellow, and DISPLAY stays at 0. The manual's "red flashes" count determines the wire. Given the light is toggling color (not just red), I think "red flashes" means the number of times the light flashed red before going dark. Since display stays 0, and light hasn't gone dark yet, flashing may still be in progress, but it's been many turns with no dark state reported. Given the persistent 0 display, I think the flash count is 0 — meaning display literally shows the flash count, and 0 flashes → blue wire.

Wire 2 is blue per Deaf's report. So I need to send two-symbol tally to mean wire 2.

I already sent two taps twice, but Deaf reported not receiving/understanding earlier ones (turn ordering delay). Let me resend clearly now that the code is confirmed mutually.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝"])
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Board now: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT is dark now (new state, was yellow then red then yellow). Wires unchanged: 1 yellow 2 blue 3 red. Mute has sent the same gesture two turns running regardless of light color - two identical tap symbols. My best guess is this means wire 2. Blind, if you have other confirmation from the manual via Mute, prioritize that, but if you need to act, wire 2 blue is my tentative read.

The light has now gone dark, meaning the flashing is officially over. Deaf reported light sequence: yellow, then red, then yellow, then dark. The manual counts "red flashes" - only red counts, not yellow. From what Deaf has reported, the light was red only once during this whole sequence (yellow, red, yellow, dark). So red flashed 1 time.

Per the manual: 1 red flash → red wire.

Wire 3 is red according to Deaf's wire color report (1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red).

I need to correct my earlier guess — my previous two-tap signal (wire 2) was sent before the light went dark and the flash sequence completed. Now that flashing is over, I can compute the correct answer: 1 flash = red wire = wire 3.

I should gesture three taps to indicate wire 3, and this is urgent since Blind may be about to act on the wrong wire 2 guess.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝"])
wait()
```
